review_notes: I read the whole file and the Mathlib HomogeneousLocalization simp API for Away.mk, Away.val_mk and Away.map_mk. I also checked the PointChart definitions xOverZ, yOverZ and zChartι. The file has no @[simp] attributes of its own. I looked for local lemmas that are really simp interface for awayCongr, scal and Away.mk, and for rewriting that is brittle at the use sites. I did not run Lean, so the suggested simp-tagging is untested. In particular, whether simp can use awayCongr_mk once hs' is removed is unchecked. I found no rewrite cycle or competing simp rules. Both findings are modest, and the second is mainly about readability.

findings.excerpt: awayCongr 𝒜 e (Away.mk 𝒜 hs n x hx) = Away.mk 𝒜 hs' n x hx
findings.problem: awayCongr is an opaque, tactic-defined equivalence (`subst e; exact RingEquiv.refl _`), so its only computation rule is this lemma. It is not tagged @[simp]. The extra hypothesis `hs'` does not occur in the left-hand side, so as stated the lemma could not be used by simp even if it were tagged. The only use site, `hmapi` (lines 216–222), therefore has to rewrite by hand: `rw [RingHom.comp_apply, Away.map_mk, RingEquiv.toRingHom_eq_coe, RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom, awayCongr_mk _ e (φ.2 hZ) hZ']`. Mathlib's analogous `Away.map_mk` is @[simp] and builds its proof argument from the data (`map_mem g hf`). The same gap shows in `awayι_eq_specMap_awayCongr_comp`, which needs an ad hoc `have : (awayCongr 𝒜 (rfl : s = s)).toRingHom = RingHom.id _ := rfl` because no simp lemma says that awayCongr along a reflexive equality is the identity.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma so that it fits simp. Drop `hs'` and produce the proof on the right-hand side from `e ▸ hs` (or `by subst e; exact hs`), then tag it @[simp] like `Away.map_mk`. Add a companion lemma saying that awayCongr along `rfl` is `RingEquiv.refl _`, together with its coe/toRingHom form, and use it in awayι_eq_specMap_awayCongr_comp. Then `hmapi` should reduce to something like `simp [RingHom.comp_apply]`, since `Away.map_mk` is already @[simp]. If a `hs'`-carrying version is still needed, keep it under a separate name.
findings.benefit: The bookkeeping equivalence awayCongr becomes transparent to simp next to Away.map_mk and Away.val_mk. The hand-written rw chain with its coercion-unfolding lemmas can then be replaced by one simp call, and later chart computations would not need to repeat the proof-term plumbing.

evidence.excerpt: Away.map g f (.mk 𝒜 hf n x hx) = .mk ℬ (map_mem g hf) n (g x) (map_mem g hx)

findings.excerpt: cls W (MvPolynomial.C a) ∈ projModelGradingCR W (0 • 1) := by
findings.problem: The statement of cls_C_mem is written with the grading index `0 • 1`, which is not in simp normal form (simp reduces it to `0`). The proof has to normalise first with a non-terminal `simp at h__af` and then `exact h__af`. The same index shape recurs as `projModelGradingCR W (1 • 1)` in the hypotheses of awayMk_X and awayMk_Y (lines 93 and 106) and in hmapi (line 216). Any `simp` or `simpa` that touches these hypotheses changes them to `projModelGradingCR W 0` or `W 1`, so they no longer match syntactically. This is also why `fromZeroRingHom_eq_mk` needs `by simpa using r.2`. For cls_C_mem there is no reason to expose `0 • 1`.
findings.proposed_change: State cls_C_mem at the normal form `projModelGradingCR W 0`. The `Away.mk` call site accepts it up to definitional unfolding of `0 • 1`, and `scal` can pass the proof as `cls_C_mem W a`, or `by simpa using …` if needed. Replace the bare `simp at h__af; exact h__af` by `simpa using h__af`. Where `Away.mk` forces the `n • d` shape (awayMk_X, awayMk_Y), keep it only in the binder type and avoid restating it elsewhere.
findings.benefit: The lemma statements use the same normal form that simp produces, so downstream `simpa`/`simp` steps do not mismatch on `0 • 1` versus `0`. The proof no longer has a non-terminal `simp`, which is fragile under changes to the simp set.
